1. This revision is directed against the impugned order dated 23.2.2023, passed by the court of Ms.
Arushi Parwal, Ld. Metropolitan Magistrate, North East District, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi,
passed in case, bearing CR Case No.2780/2018, registered vide FIR No.182/2017 PS Gokul Puri,
vide which the said court was pleased to dismiss the discharge application filed on behalf of the petitioners herein and passed the order on charge, holding thereby, that there was sufficient ground to proceed against the accused persons (revisionists herein) in respect of offences punishable under sections 498-A and 406 r/w. Section 34 of IPC.

sentences.text: 1 2. Feeling aggrieved with the said order dated 23.2.2023, the petitioners herein have filed the present revision petition.
3. The notice of the revision petition was issued to the respondent no. 2, 3, 4 & 5 and on completion of the service of notice, respondents had appeared alongwith their counsel.
4. The record of the Trial Court requisitioned and perused.
5. I have already heard the counsels for the parties.

6. Sh. Puneet Kumar Saxena, Ld. Counsel for the petitioners submitted that on the complaint u/s.
154(2) of CrPC filed on behalf of Smt. Sunita (wife of respondent no.2 herein) in CAW Cell, an FIR No.182/2017 u/s. 498-A/406/34 of IPC PS Gokul Puri was registered against the accused persons namely Sachin Awana, Subhash Chand Awana, Karmawati, Naveen Awana and Arun Awana
and after completion of the investigation, chargesheet u/s. 498-A/406/34 of IPC was filed against all the abovenamed accused persons.

During trial, an application for seeking discharge was filed on behalf of the accused Subhash, Karmawati and Naveen and thereafter, vide order dated 23.2.2023, the Ld.
Trial Court pleased to pass order on charge/discharge against the accused persons.
7. Ld.

Counsel for the petitioners further submitted that the Ld. Trial Court failed to exercise its judicial discretion on the facts and circumstances of the case by framing the charges without taking into account the correct and true facts and circumstances in entirety and considering the material evidence on record to see whether the prima facie case is made out or not causing grave injustice to the revisionists.

The trial court also failed to appreciate the fact that the pleadings and documents relied upon by the prosecution were a result of manipulative practices wherein there was a misuse of the provisions of law under Section 498A of the Act.
8. Ld.
Counsel for the petitioners further submitted that the Ld. Trial Court has framed charges ignoring the factum that whether the ingredients required under Section 498A of IPC are satisfied or not.

Further, the IO by false implication of the omnibus allegation made in matrimonial dispute was remained unchecked and the chargesheet was filed resulting into the act of misusing the process of law, which also led to causing substantial failure and miscarriage of justice to the revisionists.
9. Ld.

Counsel for the petitioners further submitted that the Ld. Trial Court also failed to appreciate that the proceedings were initiated raising allegations on the basis of the material evidences which did not support the case of the complainant on the basis of complaint.
However, the offence was never alleged to have been committed.

As such in absentia of sufficient evidence to proceed against the revisionist, the chargesheet does not disclose complete ingredients of the alleged offences and thus, no offence is made out as per the chargesheet.

Counsel for the petitioners further submitted that the Jewellery/Istridhan were always in possession of the complainant since she was living separately and further she had taken away all the jewellery and belonging with her, therefore the ingredients of Section 406 of IPC is neither satisfied nor there is any false and wrong committed on the part of the revisionists and this fact was brought Naveen Awana vs State on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52958649/
2 to the notice of the Ld. Trial Court, which was ignored in totality.
Counsel for the petitioners further submitted that the Ld. Trial Court also failed to determine whether the prima facie case is established depending upon the peculiar facts of the case.
It has been argued that the allegations pertain to the year 2009, thus the complaint was barred by limitation.

Further, it is evident that there have not arisen any grave suspicion which could establish that the prima facie case is made out and further submitted that at the stage of Section 227 and 228 IPC, the court is required to evaluate the material and documents on record with a view to find out if the facts emerging therefrom taken at their face value disclose the existence of all the ingredients constituting the alleged offence, but, the court below has failed to consider the aforesaid principle.
Hence, the impugned order suffers from material irregularity and is patently illegal and is liable to be set aside.

12. He has relied upon the judgments, Dablu Kujur v. The State of Jharkhand, 2024 (3) SCALE 657;
Sharif Ahmed & Anr. v. State of Uttar Pradesh & Anr., AIR 2024 SC 2420; Vikas & Ors. v. State (NCT of Delhi) & Anr., Crl. A. 86/2007 dated 18.1.2016, Kanchan Kumar v. State of Bihar, Criminal Appeal No. 1562 of 2022 decided on 14.9.2022; Shipali Sharma v. State of NCT of Delhi, Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 994/2013 decided on 18.8.2022 and Mohd. Haroon v. State of U.P.,
Application No. 1558 of 2023 decided on 16.1.2023.
13.

sentences.text: On the other hand, Sh. J. P. Bansal, Ld. Counsel for the complainant/respondent no. 5 has submitted that the present revision petition is not maintainable and submitted that the Ld. Trial Court has rightly passed the order on charge against the accused persons considering overall facts and circumstances of the case and prayed for dismissal of the present revision petition filed by the petitioners.
14. I have given thoughtful consideration to the submissions made by the parties and perused the record.
15. The bare perusal of the record of the Ld. Trial Court

reveals that an FIR No.182/2017 u/s.
498-A/406/34 of IPC PS Gokul Puri was registered against the accused persons namely Sachin Awana, Subhash Chand Awana, Karmawati, Naveen Awana and Arun Awana and after completion of the investigation, chargesheet u/s. 498-A/406/34 of IPC was filed against all the abovenamed accused persons.

On dated 02.12.2022, an application for seeking discharge of the accused Subhash,
Karmawati and Naveen was filed.
Vide order dated 23.2.2023, the Ld. Trial Court was pleased to dismiss the said application and passed the order on charge against the accused persons.

The observations made by the Ld. MM are reproduced as under:-
"5.
The accused persons have denied the said allegations and have brought forth their defence.
However, falsity/ proof of allegations as well as proof of defence is a matter of trial.
Simply because MLC of complainant in respect of violence is not there, the same does not become a ground for discharge.
Hence, there is sufficient ground to proceed against the accused persons in respect of offences punishable under Sections 498A and 406 r/w Section 34 IPC.

Accordingly, applications seeking discharge stand Naveen Awana vs State on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52958649/
3 dismissed.

16.

It is now well settled that at the stage of framing the charge, enquiry must necessarily be limited to deciding if the facts emerging from such materials constitute the offence with which the accused could be charged.
The Court may peruse the records for the limited purpose, but it is not required to marshal it with a view to decide the reliability thereof.
17. At the stage of framing the charge, the Court has to prima-facie consider whether there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.
The Court is not required to appreciate the evidence and arrive at the conclusion that the materials produced are sufficient or not for conviction of the accused.
If the Court is satisfied that a prima facie case is made out for proceeding further then a charge has to be framed.

18. The scope of revision is to set right a patent defect or an error of jurisdiction or law or the perversity which has crept in the proceeding; (State of Rajasthan Vs. Fatehkaran Mehdu, AIR 2017 SC 796).

Object of this provision is to set right a patent defect or an error of jurisdiction or law; (Amit Kapoor Vs. Ramesh Chander, (2012) 9 SCC 460).
19.

sentences.text:
I have also gone through the judgments relied upon by the Ld. Counsel for the petitioner, but,
the facts and circumstances of those cases are totally different from the facts and circumstances of the present case, so, same are not applicable in the case in hand.
20. So far as the order on charge dated 23.2.2023 passed by the Ld. Trial Court is concerned, this court is unable to find any illegality, infirmity or irregularity in the said order.

21. Bare perusal of the chargesheet wherein the complaint of the complainant has been reproduced,
clearly shows that there are specific allegations against all the accused persons regarding demand of dowry.

As per the chargesheet itself, the marriage between the complainant and accused no. 1 was solemnized on 11.12.2009 and after few months of marriage, the complainant was harassed by the accused persons for illegal demand of dowry.
On 12.12.2014, all the accused persons made pressure upon the complainant to bring an amount of Rs.10 lakhs from her parental home.
When the complainant failed to fulfill the illegal demand of Rs.10 lakhs made by the accused persons, on 22.10.2014, the accused persons sold out the Scorpio car, which was presented in the marriage.
Thus, the allegations made by the complainant are clear and specific enough, which prima facie show involvement of all the accused persons in commission of the alleged offences.

Trial Court.
The argument that the complaint was barred by limitation is not tenable as the allegations are there with respect to the period of 2014-2015 also.
Rest of the arguments raised by the Ld.
Counsel for the revisionists are matter of trial, which can be decided only after appreciation of the evidence.
22. In view of the above, the present revision petition stands dismissed, being devoid of merits.
23. File be consigned to Record Room.
